rationale: Two findings require fixes before approval. (1) Tailwind preflight applies list-style:none which causes Safari+VoiceOver to strip the list role — add role="list" to both <ul> elements. (2) In OnboardingToursSection the <li> becomes the grid item, breaking the align-self:stretch that previously made cards in the same row share height — add className="flex" to <li> so OnboardingFlowCard stretches via flex child behaviour. All four acceptance criteria pass.

business_review.notes: HelpSection.tsx wrapping div replaced with ul; each HelpItem wrapped in li.
OnboardingToursSection.tsx wrapping div replaced with ul; each OnboardingFlowCard wrapped in li.

business_review.criterion: key prop moved from child component to the li wrapper
business_review.notes: Both files: key removed from child component, placed on li element.

business_review.criterion: Tailwind classes preserved on the ul element
business_review.notes: flex flex-col gap-2 and grid sm:grid-cols-2 gap-3 carried over unchanged.

standards_review.notes: No HTML sinks, redirects, or secrets involved.

findings.problem: Tailwind preflight sets list-style:none on <ul>. Safari + VoiceOver removes the list role when list-style:none is present without an explicit role attribute, silently voiding the accessibility fix on Apple devices.
findings.impact: Screen reader users on Safari/iOS do not hear "list, N items" — the primary goal of this ticket is not achieved on those platforms.
findings.recommendation: Add role="list" to both <ul> elements in HelpSection.tsx and OnboardingToursSection.tsx.

findings.problem: In OnboardingToursSection the <li> is now the grid item. Previously OnboardingFlowCard received align-self:stretch directly from the grid and matched height with its row partner. Now the <li> stretches but OnboardingFlowCard inside it sizes to content, so cards with unequal content no longer share row height.
findings.impact: Visual regression: in a 2-column row where one card has more text than the other, card heights diverge.
findings.recommendation: Add className="flex" to the <li> so OnboardingFlowCard stretches as a flex child to fill the <li> height.
